entities.name: Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Shams ad-Dīn ʾAbū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʾAbī Bakr ibn ʾAyyūb az-Zurʿī ad-Dimashqī al-Ḥanbalī, commonly known as Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah or Ibn al-Qayyim for short, or reverentially as al-Imam Ibn al-Qayyim in Sunni tradition, was an important medieval Syrian Arab Islamic jurist, theologian, and spiritual writer. Belonging to the Hanbali school of Fiqh, of which he is regarded as "one of the most important thinkers," Ibn al-Qayyim was also the foremost disciple and student of Ibn Taymiyyah, with whom he was imprisoned in 1326 for dissenting against established tradition during Ibn Taymiyyah's famous incarceration in the Citadel of Damascus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent student and disciple of Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya played a crucial role in shaping Islamic theology and jurisprudence during the 14th century. His writings had significant regional impact on Hanbali scholarship and influenced subsequent generations of scholars.
